verdict.rationale: Godot ships extensive first-party docs (GDScript and C# guides, API references, asset/import docs) implying decent documentation coverage, but the primary scripting language (GDScript) is a bespoke, engine-specific language rather than a mainstream one, meaning LLMs have seen far fewer public examples of it than of Python/JS/C++; community reports corroborate this, noting GDScript is comparatively under-documented/idiosyncratic (godot-comm-15, godot-comm-13) and that C# in Godot is 'second class' with fewer examples than GDScript (godot-comm-5), and that third-party language bindings are immature (godot-comm-14). No evidence (first-party or hands-on) speaks directly to LLM code-generation success rates. missing for 10: direct evidence of LLM-generated GDScript/C# code working reliably on first try, independent benchmarks or hands-on AI coding reports, resolution of the niche-language/training-data gap noted by the community.
